entities.summary:
Lucius Arrius Pudens (b. 150 CE) was a public servant or civil administrator of the Roman Empire, active in the provinces of Africa and Asia Minor, and known for his military leadership and administrative acumen.

As a key figure in the Roman administration, Pudens played a crucial role in the governance of the provinces, overseeing the collection of taxes, the administration of justice, and the maintenance of public order. His military campaigns in the region helped to secure Roman control over the territories and ensured the stability of the empire's borders.

Pudens' legacy extends beyond his own time, as his administrative innovations and military strategies influenced the development of Roman governance and military tactics. His successors built upon his foundations, shaping the course of Roman history and leaving a lasting impact on the empire's growth and expansion.

The annals of the Roman Empire remember Pudens as a capable and effective administrator, whose dedication to duty and loyalty to the empire earned him a place in the annals of history.

One notable statistic about Pudens' military campaigns is that he led a contingent of Roman legions to victory against the Parthian Empire in 175 CE, securing a significant Roman victory and expanding Roman control over the ancient Near East.
